title: This Steering Wheel Isn't Connected to the Wheels #shorts

scenes.text: Turn this steering wheel, and nothing solid connects it to the tires. No shaft. Just wires.
For a century, a steel shaft linked your wheel to the tires. Infiniti went electronic in twenty thirteen, but kept a backup clutch.
Tesla's Cybertruck threw the backup away: two motors on the steering rack, plus a third sensor as a tie breaker.
Why? Software can change the ratio: small turns in a parking lot, calm at highway speed.
And with no shaft, a car can drop the wheel entirely, like Tesla's Cybercab.
And since July first, China allows it too: no mechanical link needed, if the backup systems meet strict rules.
So: software steering, or keep the steel? Tell me below. Follow EV Drive.
